summary: Medway Head light at the mouth of Port Medway harbour, Nova Scotia: first lit 1851, kept by the Perry family, now a 1983 tower owned by a society (sources date the transfer 2014 or 2017).

structures.type: square wood dwelling, white, black square daymark
square two-storey dwelling with lantern on its roof; moved in 1980
white square tower with red upper portion

access.note: Owned by the Medway Head Lighthouse Society. The 1983 tower is open for tours on set summer days (Rowlett). The 1927 house across the road is a private dwelling.

visit.tours: Mondays, Wednesdays, Saturdays and Sundays, 29 June to 15 September, and daily during the late-August arts and crafts show (Rowlett)

facts.agency: Medway Head Lighthouse Society (owner; LF dates a transfer ceremony to 11 June 2014, Rowlett gives June 2017)

events.note: Station established 1851; square wood dwelling 23 ft (7 m) high (NSLPS)
The name Port Medway Lighthouse moved to the wharf tower in the town; the headland light became Medway Head
Square two-storey dwelling with a lantern on its roof replaced the first light
Fibreglass tower installed. NSLPS gives 1963; Lighthouse Friends gives 10 April 1966; Rowlett gives 1966 to 1983.
1927 house sold to Alden Wamboldt of Massachusetts, who had to remove it
1927 house moved. Lighthouse Friends: a short distance to a hill above the station. NSLPS: across the road.
Wooden pyramidal tower replaced the fibreglass tower on 19 April 1983
Station de-staffed after the retirement of Douglas Smiley (LF). NSLPS: automated by 1987.
Restoration began in the fall of 2015, funded by contributions and the National Trust
Medway Head Lighthouse Society took ownership in June 2017
LF: a ceremony on 11 June 2014 celebrated the transfer of the tower and property to the Medway Head Lighthouse Society. The Rowlett directory gives June 2017 for ownership.

corrections.why: The Coast Guard List of Lights gives the Medway Head light (CCG 415, Admiralty H3722) at 44 06 10.6 N, 064 32 23.3 W, which is 44.102944 N, 64.539806 W. The record's point is an OSM position about 70 m away. Lighthouse Friends' 1927-house page gives the same 44.102944, -64.539806.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's 'inactive' (Rowlett) describes the 1927 house, which Rowlett lists as inactive as a light since 1966. The 1983 tower is active: the Coast Guard list gives Fl W 12s and NSLPS says it is operational. The station is active.
The two build dates in the record are different structures: 1927 is the dwelling later sold and moved; 1983 is the wooden tower standing now.
NSLPS gives 1963, Lighthouse Friends gives 10 April 1966, and Rowlett gives 1966 to 1983. The sources do not reconcile the dates.
Lighthouse Friends says it was moved a short distance to a hill overlooking the station; NSLPS says it was moved across the road.
Lighthouse Friends dates a transfer ceremony to 11 June 2014; the Rowlett directory gives June 2017 as the date the society took ownership. The story gives both.

LF's text dates the de-staffing to 1986 (three years after the 1983 tower); LF's keeper list ends Doug Smiley in 1987; NSLPS dates automation to 1987. The story gives the LF text date and notes the list.
LF names Isaac K. Perry as first keeper. An uncited, unread local archives post names Elson Perry (1830 to 1895) instead. The story attributes the Isaac Perry claim to LF and does not use the post.

notes_for_editor: Canadian station, so no USLHS roster. Keepers and early history come from LighthouseFriends (LF), which is copyrighted: facts paraphrased, one short quotation at most in the story. LF's 1874 inspection (H. W. Johnston's report) and the 1850 legislative grant are not in the local corpus (it starts in 1900), so they are cited as LF quotes them. Access: the record says 'private' (from LF's 1927-house page, which says the lighthouse is privately owned with grounds and tower closed). The Rowlett directory and LF's 1851-tower page both say the 1983 tower is open for summer tours on set days. The story follows Rowlett; check the Society's current schedule. First keeper: LF names Isaac K. Perry (1851 to 1853). A local archives social-media post (not read, not cited) gives Elson Perry (1830 to 1895) as the first keeper. Unresolved. Marine annual reports (fiscal 1900 to 1924): Medway head appears in station lists in 1913, 1915 and 1923, but no keeper line could be matched to it by position. The 1911 appointments table has 'Medway Head, Wm. Atkins, Nov. 22' with no year, and 'Port Medway ... Wm. P. Atkins 1909' for the wharf tower; not used. Spelling: LF and the Coast Guard spell it Wamboldt; the NSLPS plaque and Rowlett have Wambolt. Smiley (kept to 1986, ended after 1960): named only in his public role; LF's details about his family omitted. Chronicling America: 'Port Medway' searches return unrelated pages; no station-linked hits. Record conflicts: the 'status' conflict is about the 1927 house, not the lit tower. Suggest checking the NSLPS characteristic history (1941 fixed white, 1992 flashing white, 1990 electric lantern) against the Coast Guard list. Fact-check 2026-10-28: the story no longer names Smiley's wife or the plaque donors (service after about 1960, living-person rule); the 1980 buyer of the 1927 house is now unnamed. The six keepers in LF's keeper list between Elson Perry and Doug Smiley were added to this roster, including 'Mrs. William Atkins', a woman keeper named by LF with her husband's surname only.
